analysisHtml:
14 Oct thesis Short — speaking analysis

YouTube Short (2:03), filmed while driving. Explaining anomaly detection and the thesis. Speech ends at 1:49, followed by 13 seconds of silence.

Verdict

Strength: near-zero fillers (about one “uh” and one “so”, no “like” or “yeah”). You pause instead of filling, and your endings land, with pitch mostly dropping. The one note: open with the thesis line and say each sentence once.

Structure (3/5)

A clear order: anomaly detection definition → what an anomaly is (a point outside the distribution that stands out) → thesis (grammatical evolution builds structures that make anomalies easier to detect, using measurable syntax). The thesis comes last, though, and it takes a 19-second restart (1:03–1:22) to reach it.

Delivery (3/5)

  • Restarts at 0:04, 0:18, 0:35 and 0:56, plus the big one from 1:03 to 1:22.
  • Pauses rather than fillers.
  • Volume is moderate and steady but softens before pauses (3/5). Ending pitch mostly drops, which is good (4/5).
  • Ends at 1:49, then 13 seconds of silence. Cut the recording at the last word.

Authority (3/5)

Endings that drop sound sure. The restarts and the late thesis take that certainty away.

Communication levels

VoicePretty goodSteady volume, endings drop, almost no fillers; softens before pauses
BodyRookieEye contact split with the road, low energy; natural smile at 0:31
WordsPretty goodClear definition → anomaly → thesis order

Model line

"My thesis uses grammatical evolution to build structures that make anomalies easier to detect."

Redo

Answer “What is anomaly detection?” in two clean sentences.
